text.tspan: We can also compute the Fisher information rate gain from this nonlinear dependence of
local concentration on background concentration, highlighted by the term in read.
A single promoter can produce a strong peak in Fisher rate. This means that in principle, the
effect of condensation on its own would be sufficient to explain high concentration sensitivity.
Condensation is a double-edged sword, however, because outside the range of amplification
it actually reduces sensitivity. If the sphere is attractive enough, it can even dampen the
signal across all concentrations, which is unproductive.
